transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-04-25
- Time: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
- Attendees: Jesse Alvarez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Haven Head of ML), Tom Chen (Haven Platform Eng), Aisha Patel (Haven Product), Liam O'Connor (Haven Data Privacy)

Auto-generated Summary (short):
Redwood demo of Evaluation / Quality Monitoring (Console + API + Optimize). Focus on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparison workflows for an upcoming pilot. Customer concerns: PII handling, SOC2 / KMS, how regression alerts map to prompt sets, and how A/B compares across model variants and quantization. Next steps: security docs, pilot tenant, and prompt set ingestion.

Topics covered:
- Overview of Eval & Quality Monitoring features in Redwood Console
- API-driven prompt set ingestion and evaluation pipelines
- Regression alerts, baselining, and thresholds
- A/B comparisons and control groups across model variants / quantized builds
- Data residency, KMS, and audit logs for pilots
- Pilot scope and success metrics

Action items (captured above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining; quick round of intros, I'm Jesse Alvarez, I'm the AE on this.
[00:07] Marta: Hi Jesse, Marta ruiz here, Head of ML at Haven. We're mostly focused on quality monitoring across our chat/triage assistant.
[00:12] Tom: Tom Chen, infra / platform. We'll handle the sandbox and networking bits.
[00:16] Aisha: Aisha Patel, product, looking at acceptance criteria and rollout timing.
[00:20] Priya: Priya Nair, SE at Redwood, I will walk through the console and the API flows.
[00:24] Liam: Liam O'Connor, privacy. I'll ask about encryption and retention.

[00:30] Jesse: Cool. Brief agenda: demo console -> show API prompt set ingestion -> show regression alerts and A/B reports in Optimize -> discuss pilot and next steps. Sound good?
[00:36] Marta: Sounds great, we have about 45 to 60 minutes.

[02:05] Priya: Ok jumping into the console, this is the Eval / Quality page. You can see a list of prompt sets on the left, each prompt set can be tagged (e.g., triage_fallbacks_v1). We support CSV/JSON upload or API ingestion.
[02:20] Marta: Does the ingestion preserve metadata like user cohort and traffic weighting? We want to run A/B where 20% see model A, 80% model B.
[02:26] Priya: Yes you can include cohort fields in the prompt metadata; the API ingestion accepts a cohort key. The console also has a traffic-split UI if you prefer non-API.
[03:12] Tom: How are tokens and PII handled in these prompt uploads?
[03:18] Priya: By default the system can mask PII during ingest - we offer redaction rules and can optionally route uploads to a private tenant if you need no data to go through hosted transient storage. For pilot we can set your tenant to VPC/private mode.
[04:00] Liam: We need encryption at rest with our KMS. Are audit logs accessible for every eval run?
[04:07] Priya: Yes we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments and we stream audit events to your SIEM; logs include eval id, prompt set id, model variant, and timestamp.
[04:20] Jesse: Quick note, SOC2 and ISO docs are in the security pack we'll send.

[06:10] Priya: Back to the demo: here's prompt set detail; you can annotate expected outputs, add rubric checks and pass/fail criteria. We support multiple rubric types - exact match, regex, semantic similarity (embedding thresholds), and custom JS scoring.
[06:40] Marta: For semantic similarity, is that configurable per prompt? We have different acceptance thresholds per intent.
[06:45] Priya: Yep, threshold per prompt or per prompt-group. You can also attach weighted metrics so some prompts contribute more to the overall regression score.

[08:00] Priya: Now the regression alerts UI - we take a baseline window (e.g., last 7 days or your chosen baseline) and compute delta on metrics like pass-rate, median BLEU-ish score, latency distribution, and hallucination flags. You set thresholds and the system will create alert incidents.
[08:28] Tom: If we roll a quantized model build for cost savings, can we automatically compare that build to the baseline and roll back if regression > X%?
[08:35] Priya: Absolutely. The rollout policy can include automatic fallback: if regression on the critical prompt set exceeds your threshold, traffic shifts back to previous variant. We also emit a detailed comparison report.
[09:00] Marta: Example - we want to run A/B where model-A is non-quantized and model-B is 4-bit quantized. We need per-prompt pass rate and a summary that shows statistically significant difference.
[09:12] Priya: The A/B report shows per-prompt pass rates, 95% CI, and p-values for difference. It also surfaces samples where the two models disagree side-by-side and links to eval traces (raw tokens, timestamps).

[11:45] Jesse: We occasionally run offline scoring too, is there a way to ingest historic logs?
[11:50] Priya: Yes, batch ingest via API/CSV and you can re-score using new rubrics. We keep eval history so you can trend over months.

[14:10] Marta: On metrics - latency distribution matters for us, but we also track answer quality buckets. Can latency thresholds be part of regression alerts?
[14:18] Priya: Yes, you can combine conditions: e.g., trigger alert if pass-rate drops >5% OR median latency increases by 200ms. Alerts can be AND/OR groups.

[16:00] Tom: From infra side, what does pilot networking look like? We need VPC peering and restricted egress.
[16:06] Priya: For private deployments we'll coordinate VPC peering; for hosted pilots we provide a dedicated tenant with IP allowlist. We also support customer KMS for key management. For on-prem options, we have a packaged runtime.
[17:40] Liam: Retention - audit logs and inputs. We need a retention policy of 90 days for raw prompts and 1 year for aggregated metrics. Can we do that?
[17:48] Priya: Yes, retention is configurable per tenant; raw inputs can be redacted earlier if required.

[19:30] Priya: Walkthrough of API flow now: you push a prompt set via POST /v1/evals/prompt-sets with metadata, then POST /v1/evals/run referencing the prompt_set_id and model_variant. Responses are streamed back and stored with trace ids.
[20:00] Marta: Are those trace ids linkable in the console?
[20:03] Priya: Yep click-through to raw tokens, model outputs, rubrics, and diff view for A/B.

[22:10] Priya: Demoing Optimize: Optimize suggests batching and quantization profiles for workloads based on your token distribution. It will say e.g., try int8 with 512 kv cache for lower cost, but recommends canarying with your prompt sets.
[22:40] Marta: Does Optimize simulate quality drop for suggested quantizations?
[22:45] Priya: We run internal heuristics and can run a dry-run eval against your prompt set to estimate pass-rate delta, but we recommend canary + A/B to measure real behavior.

[25:05] Aisha: For product acceptance criteria we want: 1) no increase in hallucination rate above 1%, 2) median latency increase < 150ms, 3) pass-rate drop < 3% across key prompts. How do we encode that?
[25:12] Priya: Create a policy in the regression alert UI with those thresholds tied to your tagged prompt-set (e.g., critical_intent_v1). You can have policies per environment: staging vs prod.

[27:30] Priya: Showing A/B comparison output: table with per-prompt rows, pass-rate_A, pass-rate_B, delta, p-value, and example disagreements with annotated rubric scores. You can export CSV or link to a GitHub-like review UI for product/annotators to triage.
[27:58] Marta: The disagreement examples are great, can we have annotator workflows to mark false positives and feed that back to training data?
[28:05] Priya: We have an integration where annotators can tag examples; those tags can be exported or piped to your internal training repo.

[30:10] Tom: What about cost tracking? We need per-eval and per-token cost breakdowns.
[30:16] Priya: Console shows token-level cost per eval and cumulative spend per prompt-set. For pilot we can set quotas and alerts if cost > X.

[32:20] Marta: Any gotchas with streaming responses and eval tracing? Sometimes streaming truncation causes rubric mismatches.
[32:28] Priya: We have instrumentation to capture streamed tokens and finalize traces when model completes; for partials we mark them and you can exclude stream-partial traces from pass-rate or treat them with custom rules.

[34:00] Jesse: Switching gear, let's talk timeline for pilot. Marta, what's your target?
[34:05] Marta: We'd like a 2-week canary in May, then expand in June if results are good.
[34:10] Jesse: Great. We'll provision a sandbox tenant, ingest your initial 2k prompts, run baseline, canary with quantized variant, produce A/B report and regression alerts.

[36:40] Liam: On compliance: please include data flow diagram and KMS integration detail in the security pack. We might need DPIA for EU-scope data.
[36:48] Jesse: We'll include a flow diagram and KMS notes; Priya will follow up for architecture specifics.

[38:20] Priya: Quick question for you Marta - can you share an initial prompt set and success labels by Friday? That gives us enough time to provision.
[38:28] Marta: Yes aim to send that by EOD Thursday.

[40:00] Priya: Demo wrap-up: dashboard shows alerts; you can drill into a specific incident, see impacted prompts, related model variants, and a timeline of metric changes. Incidents can auto-create tickets in Jira or PagerDuty.
[40:18] Tom: We want Jira integration for triage.
[40:21] Priya: We support Jira webhook and Slack/E-mail.

[42:50] Marta: A few clarifying Qs - when you compute semantic similarity, what embedding model do you use?
[42:56] Priya: We use a curated embedding model from our catalog; for private tenants you can bring-your-own embedding model or have the eval use an internal reference embedding for consistent baselining.

[45:00] Aisha: If we detect regressions during canary, what's the rollback mechanism? Automated shift or manual?
[45:07] Priya: Both - you can select automatic rollback if threshold breached or manual with approval workflow. The system also snapshots previous baseline variant.

[47:30] Marta: Final question on data residency - if some prompts originate from EU users, can we ensure those evals are run in EU region only?
[47:36] Priya: Yes region routing supports per-prompt metadata; you can tag and route evals to EU-only infrastructure. For private deployments, you can host entirely in your EU VPC.

[49:05] Jesse: Ok quick recap of next steps and owners...
[49:10] Jesse: Jesse will send security pack + SOC2 and KMS notes by 2025-04-30.
[49:15] Priya: I'll provision a pilot tenant and upload a test prompt set once Marta sends the file (aim by 2025-05-02).
[49:22] Marta: I'll share prompt sets and success metrics by 2025-05-01.
[49:30] Tom: We'll confirm network constraints for the sandbox by 2025-05-02.
[49:36] Liam: I'll review the DPIA and confirm if we need additional controls by 2025-05-05.

[51:00] Jesse: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in an email with links to the docs and tenant.
[51:06] Marta: Thanks all, good session.
[51:10] Priya: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
